The council received £3.528m on an original investment of £4.056m, realising a loss. Property fund dividend income has also collapsed, from £442k for the full year 2024/25 to only £120k to date in 2025/26.

Tamworth Borough Council were not eligible to remain Unit Holders in the new merged fund as this is limited to UK Pensions only.

findings.paper_title: Auditor's Annual Report 2024-25 - Tamworth Borough Council- A&G 12-11-2025
findings.headline: Prior-year governance recommendation on finance workforce planning remains unimplemented after 12 months
findings.detail: A recommendation from the 2023/24 audit to consider the LGA 'Local government finance workforce action plan for England' has not been completed. Management attributes ongoing delays to completion of the senior management restructure at Assistant Director and Head of Services levels. The LGA CFO Mentoring programme is in train for the Interim Executive Director Finance.
findings.matters: Persistent delays in implementing governance recommendations suggests challenges with management follow-through and capacity planning in the finance function
findings.figures: Recommendation outstanding for 2 audit years
findings.quote: One improvement recommendation made in 2023/24 remains outstanding... Progress has been made in addressing this recommendation; however implementation remains ongoing... Progress is being made in respect of restructure of senior management and around Assistant Director and Executive Director levels. The next level of head of services is currently going through this process. Once this is finalised then the recommendation can be processed.

findings.headline: Finance leadership capacity: Assistant Director Finance role vacant since September 2024 in a small team
findings.detail: The AD Finance position has been vacant for 12 months pending completion of the Corporate Management Team restructure and is currently out to advert, though temporary cover was provided. The report acknowledges the finance team is small with reliance on individual members. While management states the team continues to manage effectively, a year-long vacancy in critical finance leadership during a major structural change (LGR) presents a capacity risk.
findings.matters: Finance leadership capacity is essential for loan covenant compliance and managing financial performance; a prolonged vacancy in a small team suggests potential resource constraints during the council's reorganisation transition
findings.figures: 12 months vacancy since September 2024
findings.quote: The AD Finance role has been vacant since September 2024 pending finalisation of the Corporate Management Team restructure and is currently out to advert. The Council did have the temporary cover in the interim period. While the size of the finance team means there is some reliance on individual members, the team continues to manage its responsibilities effectively and maintain sound financial oversight across the Council.

news_drafts.headline: Tamworth took out no new loans in 2025/26 despite £17.2m of capital spending
news_drafts.lead:
Tamworth Borough Council took out no new loans in 2025/26, even though it spent £17.2m on capital spending (money spent on things that last, such as buildings and equipment). The figure is in the annual treasury management report (how the council borrows and invests its cash) that went to its Audit and Governance Committee on 24 September 2026.

The council's total borrowing stayed at £63.060m, unchanged from the year before. The report says the spending was paid for from the council's own cash and from capital receipts (money from asset sales), a practice known as internal borrowing. This saves interest but uses up the council's cash cushion. The report puts the gap between what the council has borrowed and what its capital spending would otherwise require at £7.158m, which it describes as an under-borrowed position.

The council says the reason was cost. In the report's words: "Due to the elevated cost of borrowing long-term, no borrowing was undertaken during the year." The papers describe the approach as a continuing strategy, not a one-year decision.
